An FBI memorandum from the Chicago office, file 44-1114, weighs a tip about James Earl Ray. The bureau's source, reported by Special Agent Rene J. Dumaine, raised a possibility: the subject had been at his brother Jerry's house in Northbrook, Illinois, in April 1967. That was a year before the King assassination.

After the murder, agents rebuilt Ray's movements month by month, hunting for help he might have had. A stay at his brother's house mattered because family shelter could explain money and hiding places. The memo records a lead in the bureau's flat language: a possibility, sourced, dated, and filed. Such memos were the raw material from which Ray's timeline was later drawn.
